title: -er and -ir verbs
topic: present tense of regular -er and -ir verbs
why: After -ar verbs, this lesson completes the regular present with -er and -ir verbs, which differ only with nosotros and vosotros. You can now say where you live and talk about your habits and simple hobbies, just before the unit review.

Comer and vivir: the other two groups

You know the -ar verbs. There are two more regular groups: verbs in -er (comer, to eat) and verbs in -ir (vivir, to live). Same principle: remove the infinitive ending and add the ending for the person.

hablar (review)comer (to eat)vivir (to live)
yohablocomovivo
túhablascomesvives
él, ella, ustedhablacomevive
nosotros, nosotrashablamoscomemosvivimos
vosotros, vosotrashabláiscoméisvivís
ellos, ellas, ustedeshablancomenviven

Look carefully at the columns: with yo, it's always -o. After that, where hablar has an a, comer and vivir have an e: hablas → comes, vives; habla → come, vive; hablan → comen, viven.

-er or -ir: only two forms change

comer and vivir are identical, except with nosotros and vosotros, where they keep the vowel of the infinitive:

-er: keep the e-ir: keep the i
nosotroscomemosvivimos
vosotroscoméisvivís
Vivimos en Lyon y comemos en casa.We live in Lyon and we eat at home.

The vosotros accents: -áis, -éis, -ís. The -ís of -ir verbs has no a or e: vivís, never \"viveis\".

", "

Today's verbs

All these verbs are regular. Spot their group from the infinitive, then apply the comer or vivir pattern.

-er verbMeaningExample
comerto eat; to have lunchComo en casa.
beberto drink¿Bebes agua?
leerto readLeemos el periódico.
aprenderto learnAprendo español.
comprenderto understand¿Comprendéis la pregunta?
correrto runCarmen corre en el parque.
venderto sellVenden el coche.
-ir verbMeaningExample
vivirto liveVivo en Lyon.
escribirto writeEscribes un mensaje.
abrirto openAbrimos la ventana.
recibirto receive, to getRecibe un correo.
compartirto shareCompartís piso.
subirto go up, to climbAna sube las escaleras.

Remember

  • leer keeps the e of its stem before the ending, which gives two e in a row for several persons: leo, lees, lee, leemos, leéis, leen.
  • \"I live in Lyon\" is Vivo en Lyon: en works just like \"in\" here.
  • In Spain, comer also means \"to have lunch\", the midday meal (eaten around two o'clock): ¿Comemos juntos? = shall we have lunch together?
  • compartir piso (to share an apartment) = to have roommates. In Spain, an apartment is el piso.

For water, say el agua: the word is feminine, but it takes el for pronunciation reasons. You'll see this again later.

", "

Talking about your habits

The present tense is used for what you usually do, as in English. Three little expressions will help you say how often:

SpanishMeaningExample
todos los díasevery dayLeo el periódico todos los días.
a vecessometimesA veces como en un bar.
muchoa lot¿Lees mucho?

Mucho goes after the verb, like \"a lot\": Ana lee mucho (Ana reads a lot). For the negative, keep no before the verb: No corro mucho.

—¿Lees mucho? —Sí, leo todos los días.—Do you read a lot? —Yes, I read every day.
—¿Dónde vives? —Vivo en Bilbao. Comparto piso con dos amigos.—Where do you live? —I live in Bilbao. I share an apartment with two friends.
A veces escribimos mensajes en español.Sometimes we write messages in Spanish.

All three groups together

You now have the whole regular present. Here's a summary to keep handy:

-ar-er-ir
yo-o-o-o
tú-as-es-es
él, ella, usted-a-e-e
nosotros-amos-emos-imos
vosotros-áis-éis-ís
ellos, ellas, ustedes-an-en-en

The most common trap: writing \"vivemos\" or \"vivéis\" for vivir. For -ir verbs, think i: vivir → vivimos, vivís.
